subject: CTO rapid add — can we swap to a 30-min exec brief + technical follow-up?
messages:
From: James Park <james.park@acme.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Cc: sarah.liu@acme.com
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Possible late add — can CTO join tomorrow morning?

Evelyn —

Quick note: our CTO (Mark Tang) will be flying in tomorrow morning and there’s a small window (10:30–11:15 PT) where he can join a demo in person. I know this is short notice — sorry for the scramble. If there’s any way to shift or compress tomorrow’s session so Mark can see the exec highlights, that would be ideal. Otherwise we can do a short 20–30 minute briefing followed by a technical deep dive with your team later.

We’re very interested in Redwood’s dedup/batching story for our embedding pipeline; would appreciate a quick executive synopsis.

James
James Park
CTO, Acme Inc.
+j.park@acme.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: James Park <james.park@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Possible late add — can CTO join tomorrow morning?

James — thanks for the heads up and that helps a lot.

Jordan / Marissa — quick callout: Acme’s CTO (Mark) can only join 10:30–11:15 PT tomorrow; they’re otherwise constrained by travel. Can we either (A) move the full demo up to 10:30–11:30 and compress slides, or (B) keep the current demo time and run a 30-minute exec brief at 10:30 with a separate deep-dive later this afternoon or next day?

If option B, I recommend: 30-min exec summary (value props, ROI, ops considerations) + 60–90m technical follow-up for SRE/ML engineers. I’ve attached a slimmed agenda and a provisional two-part plan for the customer. Also attaching the travel note James shared.

Let me know which option we can operationalize — Jordan, can you confirm availability for the two windows and whether you need a different demo environment for a shortened briefing?

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: agenda-v2.pdf (application/pdf, 92KB)]
[Attachment: flight-itinerary.jpg (image/jpeg, 48KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: James Park <james.park@acme.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Possible late add — can CTO join tomorrow morning?

Evelyn / Marissa — I can cover either option but have a standing weekly ENG sync at 11:00–11:30 PT tomorrow (hard blocker). If we move the full demo earlier, I can do 9:30–11:00 PT but would need Marissa to run the closing minutes if we overlap with my sync.

I think Option B is safer: run a tight 30-min exec brief at 10:30 that highlights (1) latency/99th percentile stability, (2) unit-cost story with batching/quantization examples, and (3) one-slide migration path. Then schedule a 75-min technical deep-dive at 15:00 PT (or tomorrow afternoon) for their ML infra and SRE.

I’ll prepare a focused exec deck (two slides + demo pointer) and can demo the reduced perf dashboard for the brief.

Quick checklist for the exec brief:
- 3 slides max (value, ops, next steps)
- Live 5-min demo snippet (latency breakdown)
- Recording + slides shared immediately after

I’ve attached the trimmed agenda we used with another customer — can repurpose.

Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: James Park <james.park@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Possible late add — can CTO join tomorrow morning?

Evelyn / Jordan — Option B sounds perfect. Mark can do 10:30–11:00 PT for the exec brief; he needs to step out by 11:15 for a logistics call. He’d appreciate the 3-slide summary and the recording. For the technical follow-up, our SRE lead (Sarah) is available at 15:00 PT tomorrow.

Please confirm minutes and I’ll block both windows on our side. Also — one ask: can you include a one-paragraph note about data retention and audit logs in the follow-up deck? That’s a procurement checkpoint for us.

Thanks,
James

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: James Park <james.park@acme.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Possible late add — can CTO join tomorrow morning? — confirmed plan and invites

James / Sarah — confirmed. We’ve scheduled the two-part plan:

1) Exec brief: 10:30–11:00 PT tomorrow — Evelyn (lead), Jordan (demo + perf snippet), Marissa (Q&A backup). Will keep to 3 slides. Recording + slides will be shared within 30 minutes of end.
2) Technical deep-dive: 15:00–16:15 PT tomorrow — Jordan (lead), Marissa (infra questions), Engineering SME on standby. Agenda will include data retention & audit logs paragraph as requested.

I’ve updated HubSpot (deal ACME-2026-045) and attached the slimmed agenda we’ll use. Calendar invites are on the way from my assistant — please accept when you see them.

Next steps for us (internal): Jordan to produce 3-slide exec pack + 5-min demo snippet by EOD today; Marissa to prep answers on procurement/data retention; I’ll add the links to the HubSpot timeline and send the invites.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[evelyn.hart@redwood.com]
